problem: Erdos #126: g(k) = max |A| with all pairwise sums of distinct elements S-smooth over k primes; conjecture log g(k) = o(k)
verdict: settled: the arm is a rediscovery of Alon-Solymosi Corollary 10 and does not improve 3*2^(k-1)

reduction.name: two-row collapse
reduction.statement: Fix distinct a,b in A. For every d in A\{a,b}, (a+d, b+d) is a pair of S-units with (a+d)-(b+d) = a-b, i.e. a solution of alpha*X + beta*Y = 1 in S-units with alpha = 1/(a-b), beta = -1/(a-b). The map d -> (a+d, b+d) is injective.
reduction.consequence: g(k) <= 2 + N_Q(k), N_Q(k) = max number of solutions of a two-variable S-unit equation over Q with |S| = k primes
reduction.uses: only that rank(M) <= 2, i.e. that any two rows of M differ by a constant vector
reduction.requires: a solution count uniform in the coefficients alpha, beta, since a-b need not be an S-unit
reduction.novelty_claim: none; elementary enough to be folklore, provenance claimed only

bounds_in_k.bound: exp(256k) for large k, from log n <= r*d^8 with d=2, r=k
does not bound |A| without further work (map from 4-subsets to solutions is not injective)

nondegeneracy.two_row_route: none. A two-term equation alpha*X + beta*Y = 1 has proper subsums alpha*X and beta*Y, both nonzero because X, Y are units. No hypothesis on A beyond a != b.
nondegeneracy.general_rank_route: exactly the Alon-Solymosi rectangle condition a_jj*a_ik != a_jk*a_ij for i<j!=k. For M_ij = a_i+a_j it expands to (a_j-a_i)(a_j-a_k) != 0, i.e. exactly the distinctness of the elements of A. It is needed because their Theorem 1 assumes m_jj not in Gamma, which fails here: 2a_j is often an S-unit.
nondegeneracy.four_element_route: X+Y-Z=1 from (a_i+a_j)+(a_l+a_m)=(a_i+a_l)+(a_j+a_m). Vanishing proper subsums would force X+Y=0 (impossible, positive), a_i=a_m, or a_l=a_j. All solutions are nondegenerate, again by distinctness.

literature.cite: N. Alon, J. Solymosi, Rank of matrices with entries from a multiplicative group
literature.relevance: Corollary 10 is this exact problem, with this exact matrix. Theorem 1: rank(M) >= (log n / r)^(1/8). Theorem 9 replaces the diagonal hypothesis by the rectangle condition.
literature.verdict: the arm was already done, qualitatively, with a much worse constant

literature.relevance: same statement for A-A contained in a small-rank group

literature.cite: J.-H. Evertse 1984, On equations in S-units and the Thue-Mahler equation
literature.relevance: ax+by=1 has at most 3*7^([K:Q]+2|S|) S-unit solutions, uniform in a,b
literature.verdict: the best available input to the two-row collapse

literature.cite: F. Beukers, H.P. Schlickewei 1996, The equation x+y=1 in finitely generated groups
literature.relevance: at most 2^(8(r+2)) solutions for rank-r groups

literature.cite: P. Erdos, C.L. Stewart, R. Tijdeman
literature.relevance: lower bound exp((4+o(1))(s/log s)^(1/2)) on the number of solutions
literature.verdict: subexponential, so it does NOT obstruct the conditional route

literature.cite: arXiv 2602.07545, Erdos-Turan theorem and Eulerian integers (2026)
literature.relevance: restates 3*2^(k-1); extends to a^2 +- ab + b^2 via a Gyory-Sarkozy-Stewart lemma

conditional_implication.statement: If N_Q(k) = exp(o(k)) then g(k) = exp(o(k)), i.e. Erdos #126 holds.
conditional_implication.converse_reason: g(k) small says nothing about N_Q(k); a unit-equation solution set need not come from a set with all pairwise sums smooth
conditional_implication.target_status: open. Upper bound exp(O(k)) (Evertse); lower bound exp(k^(1/2+o(1))) (Erdos-Stewart-Tijdeman). The lower bound is consistent with exp(o(k)).

not_settled: whether the two-row collapse is already recorded in the literature
whether simultaneous unit equations (m > 2 fixed elements) admit a bound decaying in m; no such theorem is known to us and none is cited in this literature
any bound with base below 2; not attempted, no candidate
